- When sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum, reduce forecasted price targets, especially in the first 7–10 days of the horizon.  
- If model forecast spikes sharply (e.g., >10% above recent mean) and sentiment is neutral or positive, apply a downward correction of 5–15% to avoid over-optimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of price decline), model should not over-forecast recovery; cap upward bias at 10% above recent 7-day average.  
- When sentiment history includes multiple negative entries (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), suppress any forecasted upward movement beyond 10% above prior peak.  
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in early horizon (e.g., first 5 days), adjust subsequent days downward by 2–5% to account for lagged sentiment effects.  
- For forecasts with high volatility in history (e.g., >15% range in last 18 days), apply smoothing: reduce forecast variance by 30% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
